label: Drought onset and recovery
title: Drought onset and recovery
subtitle: Weekly Drought Monitor maps up to 26 Dec 2023
source: US Drought Monitor, National Drought Mitigation Center (University of Nebraska-Lincoln), USDA and NOAA

categories.label: Long-lived drought
categories.note: in drought (D1 or worse over 25%+ of the parish) for more than 26 weeks

categories.label: Recovering
categories.note: out of drought for up to 12 weeks after being in it

categories.label: No recent drought
categories.note: not in drought for the past 12 weeks

rank.note: Ranked by weeks in drought now.

how: A parish counts as in drought in a given week when D1 (moderate drought) or worse covers at least 25% of it. The map shows how many weeks in a row it has been in drought, or how long ago the drought ended. New means 8 weeks or fewer, established 9 to 26 weeks, and long-lived more than 26. Recovering means out of drought for up to 12 weeks.
limits: It re-reads the weekly Drought Monitor maps, so it has the same limits as that layer.
The 25% rule is ours. A parish near the line can switch back and forth from week to week.
Only about 5 years of weekly maps are kept, so a count that reaches the start of the record is shown as "at least".
Being out of drought now does not mean it will stay out.

credits.text: US Drought Monitor, National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the USDA and NOAA
Parish boundaries: US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain)

chart.caption: Share of the parish in D1 or worse, last 12 weeks (red: counted as in drought)
